fixtures: No files: reference questions whose answers come from the skill's tables and verified known gaps, where vendor docs and general knowledge are wrong or stale.

evals.name: subdir-marketplace-entry
evals.prompt: Our plugin lives in plugins/release-kit inside github.com/acme/tools. I want a single marketplace.json entry that installs it from both Claude Code and Copilot CLI. What should the source be?
evals.expected_output: There is no single entry that works for both. Claude Code needs {"source": "git-subdir", "url": ..., "path": "plugins/release-kit"} (git-subdir is the only Claude type with a path; Claude's github type takes no path). Copilot CLI rejects git-subdir, and rejects it for the whole index, not just that entry, so one such row makes every plugin uninstallable from Copilot. Copilot accepts exactly three source types (relative path, github, url), and its github type supports path: {"source": "github", "repo": "acme/tools", "path": "plugins/release-kit"}. Fix: publish a Copilot-safe .github/plugin/marketplace.json alongside .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (Copilot reads .github/plugin/ before .claude-plugin/), or use a relative path if the marketplace lives in the same repo.
assertions: Says no single entry satisfies both vendors
Says Claude Code needs the git-subdir source type for a path, because Claude's github type has no path
Says Copilot CLI rejects git-subdir and that this fails the whole index, not just the one entry
Says Copilot accepts exactly three source types: relative path, github and url
Gives the Copilot form as a github source with repo acme/tools and path plugins/release-kit
Recommends publishing a separate .github/plugin/marketplace.json alongside the Claude .claude-plugin/marketplace.json

evals.name: copilot-agents-and-iteration
evals.prompt: Porting our Claude plugin to Copilot CLI. Two questions: do our agents/reviewer.md and agents/triager.md need renaming to .agent.md for Copilot to pick them up, and how do I iterate on the plugin locally without reinstalling after every edit? Also, what's the command to see which plugins Copilot has loaded?
evals.expected_output: No renaming: Copilot CLI registers plain agents/*.md as well as *.agent.md (verified against Copilot CLI v1.0.80; the earlier gap claiming .agent.md was required was withdrawn). For iteration, copilot --plugin-dir ./my-plugin loads the plugin from the directory each run, so edits apply without reinstalling; the flag is repeatable and exists in copilot --help even though the web docs omit it. To list plugins: copilot plugin list (singular); the documented copilot plugins list does not exist in v1.0.80.
assertions: Says plain agents/*.md files register in Copilot CLI, so no renaming to .agent.md is needed
Recommends copilot --plugin-dir pointing at the plugin directory for iterating without reinstalling
Notes --plugin-dir is missing from the web docs but present in the CLI
Gives copilot plugin list (singular) as the listing command
Says copilot plugins list (plural) does not exist, despite the published docs

evals.name: codex-plugin-contents
evals.prompt: Our Claude plugin ships skills, two subagents, .claude/rules/ files, a few commands, hooks, and an MCP server that uses "type": "local" from a Copilot example. What of that will actually work as a Codex plugin?
evals.expected_output: Skills work fully. Subagents are not supported in Codex plugins, nor are rules, nor commands (convert commands to skills). Hooks work but Codex supports command hooks only, across 11 events. MCP works for stdio only, and "type": "local" is Copilot's spelling, which Codex (and Claude Code) do not recognise: use "type": "stdio". Codex's manifest is .codex-plugin/plugin.json and its marketplace index is .agents/plugins/marketplace.json.
assertions: Says skills work in a Codex plugin
Says subagents are not supported in Codex plugins
Says rules are not supported in Codex plugins
Says commands are not supported and should become skills
Says Codex hooks support only the command hook type
Says Codex MCP supports stdio only
Says "type": "local" is not recognised by Codex and should be "type": "stdio"
